No files read, executed, or written; no provider-configured or device testing performed. Reported test counts (88/14/9/39/10/7) and GitHub 22 checks/12 workflows are taken as given context, not treated as proof of correctness. No attempt is made to recover or paraphrase the earlier actual-Claude follow-up's two non-blocking recommendations; all notes below are derived fresh from the code shown.
nonBlockingRecommendations: connectVideo catch can leak the connecting state for one error code: playerError now owns cleanup, but YOUTUBE_PLAYBACK_BLOCKED takes neither branch (RECORDING_CHANGED requires a truthy controller, which is null when connect() itself rejects), so no detachPlayer() runs and the previously unconditional `connecting = false` from the old catch is gone. If createYouTubePlayer can ever reject with YOUTUBE_PLAYBACK_BLOCKED, `connecting` stays true and the partially built mount keeps an iframe with no controller handle, leaving Load video gated. Not verifiable from the provided excerpts (read-along-player.mjs not supplied); recommend either clearing connecting/mount explicitly in the catch or asserting in the player adapter that connect() never rejects with that code.

F3 duration-unknown branch has no terminal state: when durationSeconds is 0 or non-finite (live stream, or a provider that never reports length), pendingStart is retained and startNotice stays 'Waiting for its length before applying the link’s start time.' on every subsequent snapshot, with no bound and no path that drops the offset. Recommend bounding the wait (e.g. on first 'playing' state or after N ready snapshots) and then clearing pendingStart with a definite notice. Related: startNotice is only cleared on a successful seek, detach, or RECORDING_CHANGED, so the 'offset was ignored' message persists in video-status after the reader has manually seeked elsewhere.

read-along-bani originalRows now pins relative order (item.id === unit.lines[linePosition]?.id, item.index === headingPosition) but never asserts the positions were exhausted. A sourceDisplayOrder that is correctly ordered yet truncated still passes, silently dropping trailing lines/headings from the rendered original. Recommend a terminal need(linePosition === unit.lines.length && headingPosition === headings.length, 'BANI_SOURCE_ORDER') unless an equivalent total-row completeness check exists outside the supplied excerpt.

Heading wording is inconsistent between surfaces for the same row: selectLine/updateTeaching announce 'source heading N of M' (where M is the combined row count, so N reads as an index into headings), while renderTiming uses 'Source heading · row N'. Recommend one phrasing (the renderTiming 'row N' form is the unambiguous one) across selected-line, teach-line-label, and the marker list.

alignment-status lost both role="status" and its polite live region (aria-live="off"), so it is now fully silent to assistive technology rather than merely quieter; the chatter problem is solved but nothing announces alignment changes even for user-initiated actions. Recommend a separate, discrete polite region updated only on explicit user actions (mark, Replay line, marker-list activation), leaving the continuously-updating text non-live. The <output id="media-time" aria-live="off"> change is correct, since output carries an implicit polite live region.

mediaTimeMs uses Math.round, so a true clock up to half a millisecond before a marker (e.g. 1.0045 s against a 1005 ms marker) activates that line early. This is below marker resolution and is not a provider-keyframe tolerance, so it is acceptable, but the direction is unpinned by tests: the new suite covers [1.004, 1004] and [1.0044, 1004] and not the .5 boundary. Recommend adding the half-millisecond case and lineAt(map, MAX_TIME_MS / 1000) exactly, so the rounding direction cannot drift unnoticed.

mediaTimeMs returning null above MAX_TIME_MS / 1000 now also makes hasClock false there, so a recording past that cap surfaces the 'recording clock is not available … reconnect' refusal rather than the older 'no marked text for this part of the recording' path. Behaviourally safe (no marker is invented), but the message misattributes the cause; worth a distinct message if MAX_TIME_MS can be reached by a real recording.
